parole.significato: grove (set of trees, shrubs and other plants, generally smaller than a forest)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Provençal bosc, from Latin boscus, from Proto-Germanic *buskaz (“bush, thicket”).

parole.significato: fortress; fortification; stronghold (a large place built to withstand attacks)
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese fortaleza, from Provençal and Old Occitan fortalessa, from Late Latin fortalitia (“fortress”), from Latin fortis (“strong”).

parole.significato: tinsel (thin strips of a glittering, metallic material used as a decoration)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Provençal auripel, from Latin aureus pellis. Cognate with Catalan oripell, Italian orpello and Old French oripel
Possibly via Provençal retalhar or influenced by its spelling; both are ultimately from Late Latin retaliātus, from retaliāre, from re- + taliō (“to cut, to prune”).
From Provençal trabuc, from Latin trabs (“tree trunk, timber, beam”).
